Certainly! Here are two hints for the given step:

**Hint 1:** Consider the properties of mean-centering in linear regression. When you mean-center the design matrix $\mathbb{X}$ to obtain $\dot{\mathbb{X}}$, the intercept term (first column) remains unchanged, while the other columns are adjusted to have a mean of zero. This transformation affects the coefficients of the linear model.

**Hint 2:** Recall that mean-centering the data does not change the relationships between the variables, only their scales. Therefore, the coefficients corresponding to the non-intercept terms in the linear regression model should remain the same before and after mean-centering, assuming full column rank.
